metadata.summary: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick focused on the "good things" his side had done despite a dismal 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening day of the new season.

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick focused on the "good things" his side had done despite a dismal 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening day of the new season. United were outfought and outplayed by a Hull side widely tipped to return to the Sky Bet Championship this season at the MKM Stadium, with two goals from set pieces giving the Tigers a richly deserved victory and their first over United in more than half a century. The loss punctured the optimism around Old Trafford at the start of Carrick's first full season in charge. messages.text: Daiquiri keeps rivals at Bay in thrilling Ebor

metadata.summary: Daiquiri Bay followed up Royal Ascot success with another lucrative victory in the Sky Bet Ebor at York.
metadata.content: York: Daiquiri Bay fends off rivals to land thrilling Ebor on the Knavesmire | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content York: Daiquiri Bay fends off rivals to land thrilling Ebor on the Knavesmire The Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay denied the Wathnan Racing-owned Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling crescendo to the Ebor Handicap at York Saturday 22 August 2026 16:53, UK Image: Daiquiri Bay and Rossa Ryan won the 2026 Ebor Daiquiri Bay followed up Royal Ascot success with another lucrative victory in the Sky Bet Ebor at York. While the four-year-old has always been a smart handicapper for Alan King, he has taken his game to another level since being gelded during the off-season, with a comeback win at Newmarket followed by his narrow verdict in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal meeting in June. King had opted to keep his powder dry for the £500,000 feature of the Ebor Festival since and was rewarded in some style, with Rossa Ryan burying his mount in midfield for much of the one-mile-six-furlong journey before making his move shortly after the home turn. Daiquiri Bay moved stylishly into contention and with the near side rail to help, dug deep in the closing stages to get the better of the Wathnan Racing-owned pair of Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling three-way finish. messages.text: Norris beats Russell to Dutch GP pole

metadata.summary: Lando Norris beat Mercedes duo George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to pole position at the Dutch Grand Prix in a hectic end to qualifying.
metadata.content: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to Zandvoort pole with Lewis Hamilton in fifth | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to Zandvoort pole with Lewis Hamilton in fifth Lando Norris claimed his second consecutive pole with a superb Q3 lap at Zandvoort to see off the challenge from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 By Nigel Chiu at Zandvoort Saturday 22 August 2026 16:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Lando Norris beat Mercedes duo George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to pole position at the Dutch Grand Prix in a hectic end to qualifying. Rain threatened to cause an anticlimax to qualifying but the track remained dry enough for the McLaren and Mercedes drivers to battle it out for top spot, with Norris edging out Russell by 0.102s and championship leader Antonelli by 0.133s. Oscar Piastri was just 0.142s off in fourth in another tight session - a continuation of the trend throughout the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort - and sets up a fascinating race on Sunday when the lights go out at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 . messages.text: Notable Speech clinches City Of York crown for Appleby

metadata.summary: Notable Speech bounced back to his brilliant best to claim his sixth Group One victory in the Sky Bet City of York Stakes.
metadata.content: York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby Charlie Appleby's Notable Speech returned to top form when rocketing to victory in the City Of York Stakes under William Buick, setting up a potential return to America for the Breeders' Cup Mile. Saturday 22 August 2026 16:01, UK Image: William Buick aboard Notable Speech Notable Speech bounced back to his brilliant best to claim his sixth Group One victory in the Sky Bet City of York Stakes. Charlie Appleby's chestnut has been a top-class performer for the last three seasons, with his big-race haul including the 2000 Guineas and Sussex Stakes in 2024, the Woodbine Mile and Breeders' Cup Mile in 2025 and the Lockinge at Newbury this spring. He suffered a rare blip when only sixth as favourite the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot in June, but dropped back to seven furlongs on the Knavesmire - albeit on easier ground than ideal - and showed his true colours in the hands of regular partner William Buick, travelling powerfully before quickening two and three-quarter lengths clear of the chasing pack as the 9-4 favourite. Appleby said: "You've got to admire him. You get good horses who can do it at two and three, but when they do it at four and five you've got to doff your cap to them. messages.text: ​​​​​Russell wins Dutch Sprint to trim title gap to Antonelli

metadata.summary: George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.
metadata.content: Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort George Russell cuts his title deficit to Kimi Antonelli to 56 points with Zandvoort Sprint win; Charles Leclerc passes Lando Norris for second; Lewis Hamilton seventh; watch Qualifying later on at 3pm with Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 14:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race. George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli. The polesitting Russell held the lead from Lando Norris at the start and and withstood an initial challenge from his fellow Briton before the McLaren fell into the clutches of Charles Leclerc's Ferrari behind. Despite being on the more brittle soft tyres compared to the mediums of those around him, Leclerc overtook Norris for second with an impressive move into the first corner on lap 18 of the short-form contest. messages.text: Antonelli to take Monza grid penalty for engine change

metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms Kimi Antonelli to incur grid penalty for exceeding engine parts at Italian GP; championship leader to face at least 10-place penalty at home race in Monza; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 16:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffered a race-ending engine failure in Barcelona World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed. Each driver is permitted a capped amount of various power unit parts for the season, and two separate technical issues for Antonelli have left Mercedes resigned to the fact the Italian will need to exceed the limit before the end of the campaign. If possible, teams will generally choose to incur grid penalties at tracks where overtaking is easier, which is why Mercedes are set to install a new power unit for Antonelli at his home race in Monza from September 4-6.
